name: DB Performance
description: Monitors slow database queries and suggests indexes to improve Drupal performance.
project_description:
DB Performance monitors slow database queries, aggregates them using query fingerprinting, and suggests indexes to improve performance without external tools.

A kernel TERMINATE event subscriber logs every request's queries via Drupal's core database logger, keeps only SELECT queries slower than a configurable threshold, normalizes each into a canonical fingerprint (literals and numbers replaced with placeholders), and stores aggregated per-fingerprint statistics (call count, average/max/total time, first/last seen, origin file/line/view) in a dedicated db_performance_query table. An admin report at /admin/reports/db-performance lists the slowest queries; when enabled, each is analyzed with EXPLAIN to detect full table scans and a CREATE INDEX statement is suggested from the query's WHERE and ORDER BY columns. Suggestions can be exported as an .sql file, and, when explicitly allowed in configuration, created directly from the UI through a confirm form. The module has no dependencies beyond Drupal core and works with MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL.

Typical uses: debugging slow pages, optimizing Views and entity queries, and identifying missing indexes on large content or e-commerce sites without New Relic, Blackfire, or other external profilers. The report needs real traffic to accumulate meaningful data, so run the site under typical usage before reviewing results.
